source.name: BBC World News RSS
source.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
source.summary: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.

lesson.title: Europe responds to an accusation
lesson.overview: Keep an accusation separate from a proven fact.
lesson.prediction: Read the title. What do you think the story is about?
discussion: What happened? Start with: The report says ___.
Think about a claim you might hear. Complete: Before I believe it, I can check ___.
news_brief_sentences: Germany has blamed Russia for a failed drone attack.
The attack was aimed at Leipzig airport.
The EU and Nato say they will put more pressure on Russia.
Russia is accused of acting more recklessly.

vocabulary.definition: said to have done something wrong

grammar.explanation: Is accused of reports a claim about wrongdoing. It does not establish that the claim is true.
grammar.example_quote: Russia is accused of acting more recklessly.

quiz.question: What place was the reported attack aimed at?
options: Leipzig airport
An EU classroom
A new railway station
option_feedback: The source identifies Leipzig airport.
A classroom is not the target identified.
A railway station is not the target identified.

quiz.question: What have the EU and Nato promised?
options: More pressure on Russia
An end to all airport travel
A new airport opening
option_feedback: The headline says they will step up pressure.
The source does not announce this restriction.
The source does not announce an airport opening.

quiz.question: What does failed describe here?
options: An attack that did not succeed
An attack that has not been planned
An attack that is certain to happen tomorrow
option_feedback: Failed means unsuccessful.
Failed does not mean unplanned.
Failed refers to an unsuccessful event, not a guaranteed future one.

quiz.question: Does is accused of mean proven responsible?
options: No. It reports a claim.
Yes. It means proof is complete.
No. It means no one made a claim.
option_feedback: Keep the allegation separate from proof.
The phrase alone does not establish proof.
An accusation is a claim; this option denies that.
